quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Eastern Conference win totals were artificially inflated by tanking teams
quotes.excerpt: all of these numbers coming off last year were artificially inflated.
quotes.quote: We can spend hours debating whether the Thunder should have had 58 wins or 64 wins or whatever, but all of these numbers coming off last year were artificially inflated by the tankers. And so, I would use that reality to guide you, not just you fine gentlemen, but as anybody thinks about this upcoming season. Certainly the playoffs were the playoffs, but remember last year that it was a sideways year when it comes to the wins.

quotes.speaker: Vince Goodwill
quotes.summary_phrase: Championship arrogance can lead to inflated regular season win totals
quotes.excerpt: you can pick up five or ten wins that maybe you don't get otherwise just because you're arrogant.

text_blocks.speaker: Vince Goodwill
text_blocks.text: It's a tricky thing, guys, because usually for me, when you win a championship, there is either the championship malaise, or there's this sort of championship arrogance that comes in where you can pick up five or ten wins that maybe you don't get otherwise just because you're arrogant as hell. And you win the game before the game even begins. You saw it, I want to say with the third year of the LeBron Miami Heat. Not saying that this is the super team of that, but once you get the validation of winning the championship and you know how you're going to play, and everything sort of clicks, right?

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: 27-game win streak or 28, whatever it was?

text_blocks.speaker: Vince Goodwill
text_blocks.text: Yeah, yeah, and they won like 66 games. I've seen teams in that second year, like everything just sort of clicks, right? But you're right that they were a third seed going into the playoffs and I think that was a reason why some people weren't as bullish as maybe we should have been, as evidenced by the playoffs.
